preposition.name: Pre-position
preposition.blurb: Sit undetected inside critical systems so access already exists when a crisis makes it useful.
preposition.how: +1 at the end of each adversary turn while it holds an undetected foothold on OT, a server, identity or data (or a crown jewel); −1 when it holds none.
preposition.lesson: Pre-positioning is a win condition for the adversary even if nothing breaks: the damage is the option value. Defenders counter it with detection of living-off-the-land behaviour and by evicting persistence, not by waiting for an incident.

access.name: Sell access
access.blurb: Establish broad, durable access across the estate to hand to ransomware affiliates or other buyers.
access.how: Breach if it holds undetected footholds on 5 different assets at the end of an adversary turn.
access.lesson: Initial access brokers monetise breadth and persistence, not data. The signal is lateral spread and new persistence, long before any ransomware appears.

exfil.name: Steal data
exfil.blurb: Collect and remove sensitive data: espionage, extortion without encryption, or resale.
exfil.how: Each successful exfiltration scores 1 (2 from a crown jewel). Reaching the target is a breach.
exfil.lesson: Exfiltration-only extortion skips encryption entirely, so backups do not help. Egress control, data classification and staging detection do.

ransom.name: Encrypt & extort
ransom.blurb: Encrypt systems and destroy recovery options to force payment.
ransom.how: Each successful impact scores 1 (2 on a crown jewel). Reaching the target is a breach.
ransom.lesson: Ransomware operators remove recovery first. Immutable, tested backups and fast containment change the economics.

destroy.name: Destroy
destroy.blurb: Irreversibly destroy data or systems: wipers disguised as ransomware, or destruction in support of a state objective.
destroy.how: Each successful destructive strike scores 1 (2 on a crown jewel). Reaching the target is a breach.
destroy.lesson: Wipers offer no decryption key and no negotiation. Recovery capability, not payment, is the control.

disrupt.name: Disrupt service
disrupt.blurb: Take down a service or the physical process: grid, water, telco, or a public-facing service.
disrupt.how: Each successful disruptive action scores 1 (2 on OT or a crown jewel). Reaching the target is a breach.
disrupt.lesson: In OT the control objective is availability and safety. Manual-operation and safe-state procedures are the real recovery plan.

fraud.name: Steal money
fraud.blurb: Reach the system that moves money (payments, SWIFT, exchange) and make a fraudulent transaction.
fraud.how: Only actions against a crown jewel score (2 each). Two successes is a breach.
fraud.lesson: Financial fraud targets the payment path and the humans who approve it. Dual control and out-of-band verification are the compensating controls.

resource.name: Hijack resources
resource.blurb: Quietly burn the victim’s compute for mining or botnet use.
resource.how: +1 at the end of each adversary turn while it holds 2 or more undetected footholds; −1 otherwise.
resource.lesson: Resource hijacking is noisy on the bill rather than on the SIEM. Cloud cost anomalies and exposed management planes are the tell.

assurance.name: Maturity Level 2
assurance.note: Adversaries start with a foothold and tools.
